name: tool-executed-evidence-receipts
title: Pin (command, selector) on verification intents and make the tool execute them instead of trusting a caller-authored pass
description:
Step 2 (M1) of the evidence-integrity program (docs/evidence-integrity-program-spec.md; handoff docs/step2-evidence-receipts-handoff.md). This is the core fix for the most frequent failure class: evidence-binding mismatch.

Problem (class ①, an interface defect not a discipline defect): when recording verification evidence the agent authors a `command` + `result:pass` that the tool cannot mechanically check against the item's declared intent, and the tool trusts it. VerificationIntentItem (packages/main/src/core/types.ts:203-212) has id/desc/type/requiredIn/priority/plannedPathDeclarations — NO command or selector field. The only binding predicate is evidenceMatches = `evidence.intentRef === ref` (packages/main/src/core/verification.ts:46-47). verification_evidence_add (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:888) accepts an arbitrary optional command+result and validates only note/kind/waiver/item-existence/hashes; it does not even check that intentRef resolves to a real intent on that item. The proof unit is (command, selector), NOT command alone: in the B-bf52 burn 16 of 19 evidence rows shared one command and what distinguished intents was a case name in free-text notes that nothing checked. This produced F-049/F-050 (wrong command), F-045 (cited a case that does not exist), F-061 (cited the wrong case within the right command) repeatedly across sessions.

The fix (this story — the enforcement floor): the tool resolves the intent, runs the declared verifier, and stamps a receipt so a false command becomes impossible, not merely caught.
1. Add an optional verification:{command,selector} to VerificationIntentItem (precedent: plannedPathDeclarations, a structured declaration already hanging off the intent item). Because the intent is frozen from DEV (checklist.ts refuse path) and at PLAN the implementation does not yet exist, this is PINNED on the FIRST evidence write for that intentRef and immutable thereafter — no PLAN-time foreknowledge needed, later drift mechanically impossible.
2. For automated intent types (logic|cli|integration), verification_evidence_add stops trusting a caller-authored command+result; it EXECUTES the pinned command via the existing validation-executor.ts spawn path (executeValidationPlan) and refuses the write when ANY of: (a) exit code != 0 but pass is claimed; (b) the selector string is absent from captured output (this single check kills F-045/F-049/F-050/F-061); (c) intentRef does not resolve to an intent on that item (today silently accepted); (d) the pinned command != the command about to run (error using the existing receipt-command-mismatch: expected X, got Y convention).
3. The receipt stores exitCode + outputDigest + outputTail (model on done-required-validation.ts:892-895), giving reviewers real numbers instead of prose claims.
4. type manual|docs cannot auto-execute: keep them as attestation, mark them explicitly non-mechanical, and do NOT score them equal to tool receipts at the gate (else manual is an escape hatch that bypasses the whole mechanism).
5. Migration/escape: grandfather existing prose-only intents (audited repair path or policy mode); do not hard-break stories mid-flight; manual/emergency overrides must be explicit, attributable, and visible to gates.

Out of scope (deferred): the verification_run ergonomic command and the PreToolUse seatbelt (follow-on story ①b); making verification_evidence_refresh_stale re-execute the pinned command (belongs with ①b; the interim laundering fix is B-3b88 / Step 1, a separate active story — do NOT touch refresh_stale here); the Step 3 review-budget breaker and Step 4 idempotent verdict writers.

Existing building blocks to reuse (do not reinvent): validation-executor.ts spawn/executeValidationPlan (isolated process group, timeout→exit 124, captures stdout+stderr); done-required-validation.ts receipt fields (exitCode/outputDigest/outputTail/commandSpec) + the receipt-command-mismatch convention; lattice-dispatch.ts command allowlist for the executor; live-smoke-transcript.ts --capture discipline (runs ONLY the given command, never derives one).
